static_traits.name: Liu Qian
static_traits.family_status: has one child; spouse supportive, but the relationship affected by the client's despair
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with spouse;Feels isolated at Family gatherings; overall social life Not mentioned in more detail
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past history of similar problems; never received other psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: clear expression, able to describe emotions and trigger situations specifically; able to cooperate with the counselor and willing to try new strategies;Positive attitude; thinking showing tendencies of 'black-and-white' 'overgeneralization' 'mental filtering' 'negating the positive'

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt that because I have only one child, my life is ruined; this triggers despair and sadness, persisting over the past few years, often triggered by Family gatherings or social media content about large families.
basic_info.core_demands: these despair feelings are affecting my daily life and overall well-being, so I come seeking counseling, hoping to get better and enjoy life more fully.
growth_experiences: intense despair and sadness began not long after childbirth and persisted in the following years; believing social expectations and pressure for multi-child families are the cause. This belief is constantly Reinforced when seeing multi-child families at Family gatherings and on social media, gradually forming the standard that 'at least Two children counts as complete/successful'; this affects Marriage and relationships, hobbies (e.g. gardening) and sleep.

core_beliefs: I am a failure/not a complete Mother
if I do not have at least Two children, I am not recognized

special_situations.event: seeing relatives' and friends' multi-child families at Family gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I have only one child, others will pity me, look down on me, I do not fit in
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Confides in his spouse, trying to distract himself by focusing on work and hobbies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not fit in, everyone must be pitying me

special_situations.event: Sees posts and pictures about large families on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: having multiple children is the norm and success, I am fated to miss out on 'normal' and 'successful'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: deliberately doing hobbies or throwing oneself into Work to reduce discomfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My life has already been ruined

special_situations.event: Moments when the relationship with the spouse is strained over this issue
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: as long as it is not Two children, it means failure and incompleteness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Invests energy into work to maintain functioning, temporarily avoiding conflict topics

special_situations.event: Thinking of society's expectations and pressure on multi-child families
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should at least Has two children, only then qualifying and being recognized
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: constantly judging oneself by external standards, ignoring existing positives (supportive spouse, joy the child brings)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have had more than one child

core_conflict.wish: longing for a more complete family, gaining the identity of a 'qualified Mother' and external recognition
core_conflict.fear: fear of being judged, pitied and excluded for not meeting social expectations, even 'life ruined'
defense_goal: Maintains a stable sense of self-worth with a rigid standard (at least two children)
avoiding the anxiety of facing uncertainty or Being rejected through harsh self-blame and negating positives

object_relations.object_representation: others/society as harsh judges (who may look down on or pity me at any time)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: when Family gatherings and others' children come up in counseling or life
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: others will pity or look down on me (Projecting inner Self-deprecation onto others' attitudes)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes in a cautious tone 'they all think I am pitiful', and uses this to avoid exploring the basis and evidence for her own feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores 'what positive evidence can refute the negative belief'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: positives are unimportant or do not count, the core belief is the fact
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Calm tone but ignores or downplays positive experiences, quickly returning to negative claims.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked 'why insist that having many children is normal' and guided to test the belief
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Social norms are right, and my sadness has legitimate reasons (explains emotions by external standards)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: using Average-style expressions (e.g. 'everyone is like this'), Interpreting based on social expectations, reducing exploration of personal experience.

manifestations: repeatedly stating 'My life is ruined' 'life is incomplete'
Positive experiences overshadowed by negative beliefs (ignoring spousal support and the joy brought by children)
Feels isolated and excluded when seeing multi-child families at Family gatherings
outcomes: alienation and Self-denial in Social situations

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes 'at least two children counts as normal / qualified' as a self-standard

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: believing 'everyone is pitying me/looking down on me' without direct evidence
In social scenes, attributes own shame experiences to others' attitudes

exception_events.target_problem: when seeing multi-child families, the client usually falls into rumination of 'life ruined' and intense sadness
exception_events.unique_outcome: At concrete moments of interacting with the child and watching the child grow and learn, the client experiences obvious joy and satisfaction, and the intensity of negative thinking decreases
exception_events.reason: different approach: focusing attention on the details and value of present parent-child interaction; different understanding: acknowledging 'the one child already brings meaning and joy'.

exception_events.target_problem: in daily life, negative emotions often interfere with leisure and sleep, causing Overall well-being impaired
exception_events.unique_outcome: in Work settings, the client stays engaged,Work performance not yet affected
exception_events.reason: different context:Work tasks are structured with clear pacing, attention focused on concrete goals, helping reduce rumination and comparison.

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse to confide in
Connection with children brings real joy and satisfaction
Stable engagement and functioning maintained at work
Willing to try new strategies and record and observe negative thoughts
negative_force: Introjecting the outside world's multi-child standards, treating them as the sole measure of self-worth
habitual thought patterns of comparison and despair
mind-reading and black-and-white thinking causing Self-denial
mental filtering and negating positive experiences
social expectations and Family gatherings/social media stimuli continuously triggering negative cognitions

target_behavior.behavior: Daily rumination on the automatic thought 'my life is ruined/I am a failure', accompanied by intense sadness
antecedent: seeing or encountering multi-child families (Family gatherings)
Browsing content about large families on social media
Thinking about society's expectations and pressure for multiple children
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting social expectations as self-standards with comparison and mind-reading, forming black-and-white and overgeneralized cognitive biases, inducing catastrophic self-statements.
target_behavior.function: venting emotions and seeking external standards in the short term to maintain control, avoiding the challenge of facing uncertainty and self-acceptance.
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension with spouse; fewer hobbies;Sleep disturbance; overall Decline in sense of well-being.
